worker_owner: worker-6 final adjudication of existing mechanism evidence
extraction_scope: Source-reviewed final mechanism ontology record from XML/PDF figures and methods. The direct mechanism is apoptosis by annexin V/7-AAD; speculative intracellular target discussion is bounded as hypothesis.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CPP-conjugated SRC-1 peptides, including TP10-SRC1LXXLL, enter MCF-7 cells and are detected in cytoplasm and nucleus after 1 h exposure.
direct_assay_types: live-cell confocal microscopy with FITC-labeled peptides
mechanism_claims.limitations: Localization supports uptake/nuclear presence but does not identify the lethal intracellular binding target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: TP10-SRC1LXXLL-treated MCF-7 cells show annexin V-positive populations at 24 h, supporting apoptosis as the main observed cell-death mode over necrosis.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The exact molecular target upstream of apoptosis is not resolved by the local source material.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The cytotoxic effect is not supported as a direct ER-mediated transcription inhibition mechanism because pS2 was not downregulated and other ER-responsive transcript changes were not specific to TP10-SRC1LXXLL.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TP10-SRC1LXXLL in MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells
mechanism_claims.limitations: This rules against the tested ER transcription readout but does not rule out all intracellular targets of the LXXLL motif.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper discusses possible non-ER intracellular protein-protein interaction targets for the LXXLL motif, but these remain mechanistic hypotheses rather than directly proven targets in the local data.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Do not promote mediator, HLH, ERα pocket occupancy, or other discussed targets to direct mechanism without additional primary assay evidence.

unresolved_or_bounded_claims: The local paper does not identify a precise upstream molecular target for TP10-SRC1LXXLL-induced apoptosis.
ER-mediated transcription disruption is not supported as the direct cause of cell death by the reported pS2/CTSD/BCL2 readouts.
